pitch: What neuroscience tells us about how the brain learns: attention, active engagement, error feedback and consolidation.
br: Being wrong in order to learn
What babies do better than AI
Make It Stick · Ericsson · Dweck · Kahneman
quiz: What are the four pillars of learning according to Dehaene?
Attention, active engagement, error feedback, consolidation
Everyone can act on these four mechanisms.
Forming an internal model of the world, adjusted through hypotheses
The brain makes hypotheses and corrects them.
Redirecting old circuits toward cultural learning such as reading
Reading recycles a visual region used to recognize objects and faces.
What happens to what we don't pay attention to?
What does the two-kitten experiment show?
A passive organism learns almost nothing
Only the active kitten developed normal spatial vision.
What is the difference between error feedback and punishing errors?
The first informs and drives learning; the second causes fear and disengagement
Assess often, with low stakes, in order to learn.
What role does sleep play in learning?
It replays and consolidates the day's learning
It even reorganizes knowledge, beyond preserving it.
More effort, but much more memory.
